Summary: Confirm mobile personas, MVP scope, supported devices, and success metrics
Description: Run a product workshop to confirm whether the first release is an internal operations app. Proposed MVP personas are installer/field employee, manager, admin, and master admin. Proposed MVP focuses on authentication, assigned lots, project/lot/stage visibility, field photos, maintenance checklists, calendar, search, and dashboard; procurement and administration are phased later.
Business Value: Prevents an expensive one-for-one desktop port and keeps the first release focused on field and operational value.
Acceptance Criteria:
Named personas and top jobs-to-be-done are approved.
MVP, Phase 2, and excluded capabilities are documented.
Supported iOS/Android minimums and tablet expectations are agreed.
Success metrics include activation, weekly active users, upload success rate, crash-free sessions, and task completion time.
Decision on public portfolio/customer-facing functionality is recorded.
Technical Notes / Risks: Working assumption for the rest of this backlog: internal business app; public marketing portfolio remains in Next.js.
Definition of Done: Implementation is reviewed; automated tests pass; iOS and Android behavior is verified; documentation is updated; Product Owner accepts the ticket.

Summary: Publish an authenticated API inventory and OpenAPI contract
Description: Document every mobile-consumed endpoint, request/response schema, authorization rule, enum, error code, multipart field, and date format. Generate an OpenAPI document and typed client artifacts for the React Native codebase.
Business Value: Reduces integration defects and makes backend/mobile work parallelizable.
Acceptance Criteria:
OpenAPI contract covers all MVP endpoints.
Examples include success, validation, unauthorized, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and rate-limit responses.
Multipart upload and byte-range media responses are documented.
Enums match Prisma values exactly.
Contract validation runs in CI and generated TypeScript types compile.
Technical Notes / Risks: Current API responses generally use {status,message,data}, but shapes and logging warnings vary.
Definition of Done: Implementation is reviewed; automated tests pass; iOS and Android behavior is verified; documentation is updated; Product Owner accepts the ticket.

Summary: Introduce versioned mobile API routes and a consistent response envelope
Description: Expose mobile contracts under a stable version prefix and standardize success, validation, pagination, and error payloads without breaking the existing web client.
Business Value: Allows the mobile app to evolve safely while the desktop app remains operational.
Acceptance Criteria:
Mobile endpoints are available under an agreed version such as /api.
Success responses use a documented data/meta envelope.
Errors include stable machine code, user-safe message, field errors where applicable, and correlation ID.
Existing web endpoints continue to work or have a documented migration path.
Contract tests cover representative endpoints.
Technical Notes / Risks: Avoid a flag-day migration of the existing Next.js frontend.
Definition of Done: Implementation is reviewed; automated tests pass; iOS and Android behavior is verified; documentation is updated; Product Owner accepts the ticket.

Summary: Consolidate and harden bearer-session validation
Description: Replace split session-validation behavior with one server-side guard that verifies token existence, expiry, active/verified user state, and current user type in a single lookup. Define revocation and device-session behavior for mobile.
Business Value: Protects company and employee data and gives mobile a predictable authentication lifecycle.
Acceptance Criteria:
One shared authentication guard is used by every protected mobile endpoint.
Expired, revoked, inactive, and unverified sessions return 401 with stable error codes.
Session lookup returns current user state rather than trusting stale session user_type.
Sign-out revokes the active token.
Tests cover valid, expired, missing, inactive-user, and revoked sessions.
Session lifetime and optional per-device session policy are documented.
Technical Notes / Risks: validateAdminAuth currently accepts admin, master-admin, manager, and employee; getUserFromToken does not itself validate expiry or active user state.
Definition of Done: Implementation is reviewed; automated tests pass; iOS and Android behavior is verified; documentation is updated; Product Owner accepts the ticket.

Summary: Enforce module-level permissions on the server
Description: Map mobile operations to module_access permissions and enforce them in API middleware. Master-admin may bypass module checks; all other roles must satisfy the required permission for both reads and mutations.
Business Value: Prevents a user from bypassing UI restrictions by calling APIs directly.
Acceptance Criteria:
A permission matrix maps each mobile route/action to a module_access field.
Unauthorized module access returns 403, distinct from unauthenticated 401.
MASTER/master-admin bypass behavior is explicit and tested.
Read, create, update, delete, upload, and administrative operations are covered.
Permission changes take effect without app reinstall and are reflected after refresh.
Technical Notes / Risks: Current granular checks are concentrated in the client-side AdminRoute site map.
Definition of Done: Implementation is reviewed; automated tests pass; iOS and Android behavior is verified; documentation is updated; Product Owner accepts the ticket.

Summary: Define mobile environment, networking, timezone, and idempotency rules
Description: Define development/staging/production base URLs, TLS requirements, device connectivity behavior, Australia/Adelaide date handling, mutation idempotency, optimistic-concurrency behavior, and correlation IDs.
Business Value: Prevents duplicate mutations, timezone drift, and environment-specific failures.
Acceptance Criteria:
No production secret is exposed through NEXT_PUBLIC or bundled mobile configuration.
All production traffic requires HTTPS.
Dates are transmitted in ISO 8601 with timezone rules documented.
Critical mutations accept an idempotency key and safely replay.
Conflicting updates return 409 with current version data or a documented resolution path.
Every request/response can be traced with a correlation ID.
Staging works from physical iOS and Android devices.
Technical Notes / Risks: The backend already contains Adelaide-specific dashboard date conversion; notification code reads a WhatsApp token from a NEXT_PUBLIC-named variable and should be reviewed.
Definition of Done: Implementation is reviewed; automated tests pass; iOS and Android behavior is verified; documentation is updated; Product Owner accepts the ticket.
